messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed Buchwald-Hartwig amination of 3-chloropyridine with 4-methylaniline; choose the ligand, base and isoxazole additive.

picks.reason: A17 gave the strongest result outside the current best condition, so testing it with the top-performing ligand and base checks whether that benefit carries over.
This tests whether A2 improves when paired with the best-performing ligand–base combination rather than the previously tested B1.
A12 has only been tested with other ligand–base combinations, making this a useful test under the current best backbone.
A1 is the leading additive, and this experiment isolates whether B2 can outperform B3 with the best ligand and additive.
This screens an untested additive under the strongest observed ligand–base pairing while exploring beyond the few additives already sampled.
